$comment: The form of the list of what holds each rule (scripts/holders.json, which scripts/holders.mjs reads; its "about" says what each part means). The keys' form, "#N" or "#N.P" beside the numbers up to the last numbered item, is archive.mjs's KEY and LAST_NUMBERED, which the holders check's own test holds this schema to. What a schema cannot say stays with the script: that a key names a rule as it stands, that a check named is there, a holder's form (its parts are read there), an item that is not in the archive, and a number's form, which outcomes.mjs builds from its lists. Each rule's mend is what a failure of it says (scripts/schemas.mjs).
title: scripts/holders.json
mend: write it as a JSON object: "holders", "behind" and "numbers", each an object keyed by each rule's file and lead, as its "about" says

about.mend: write the note as one string

holders.mend: write "holders" as an object keyed by each rule's file and lead ("floor/security.md: 1. Nothing secret in the repository")

additionalProperties.mend: write the rule's holder as "check: <its script, workflow or GitHub's setting>", "audit" or "describes", each with ", in part" where it holds only some of the rule, or a list of them

items.mend: write each holder as "check: <its script, workflow or GitHub's setting>", "audit" or "describes", each with ", in part" where it holds only some of the rule

behind.mend: write "behind" as an object keyed by each rule's file and lead, or a rule file alone, each the list of the keys of the items behind it

additionalProperties.mend: write it as a list of the keys of the items behind the rule, such as [134, "#744"]

items.mend: write an item's key as the archive keys it: its number up to 262 (a number, not a string), or "#N" for the issue that carries the owner's word, or "#N.P" for one point of it (#744)

numbers.mend: write "numbers" as an object keyed by each rule's file and lead, each the number the rule names

additionalProperties.mend: write "<findings | check fires | correction: <kind>>; outcome: <asked | fast | readable | usable | robust>", the count the rule is meant to lower and the outcome it stands for, with "; rare harm" at its end where the rule guards against rare and severe harm
